idea: The study of systems that evolve over time. It asks whether long-term behavior is predictable, random-looking, or stable. This entry studies the specific objects and conditions named in the source claim below.

A shape is convex if the straight segment between any two of its points stays inside the shape.
A mathematical statement proposed to be true but requiring proof or a counterexample.

exactClaim: Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants. Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class, even an unbounded one, has a common compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set. All positive trajectories in that class therefore eventually share positive lower and finite upper concentration bounds.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
